$$

Consider the curve ${x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x+y=3.$ Given that $x=x(t),\text{ }y=y(t),$ and that $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=7$ on the curve at the point $(1,3),$ find the value of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}$ at that point.

$\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x+y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3) \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (2x\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=7,$ $x=1,$ and $y=3,$ and solving for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (2x\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =0 \\ 7\cdot (2(1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1))+(1)^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{1}\cdot 7+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =0 \\ 0+7+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =0 \\ 7+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$
